title: GTA 6 Changes the Run Button After 25 Years
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 is changing its control scheme, finally moving away from the 25-year-old tradition of tapping a face button to sprint.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## A 25-Year Tradition Finally Comes to an End

For nearly 25 years, the Grand Theft Auto series has maintained a very specific and iconic control quirk: if you wanted your character to sprint, you had to repeatedly tap a face button on your controller. While certain past Rockstar titles offered alternative control configurations, the universal default has consistently demanded that players rhythmically tap X or A, depending on the platform.

Now, media reports from Eurogamer indicate that GTA 6 is finally bucking this long-standing trend. This upcoming shift marks a massive turning point for a control scheme that has defined open-world crime sprees for a quarter of a century.

## Modernizing the Open-World Experience

For decades, the repetitive face-button tapping method became synonymous with the franchise's movement system. While veteran fans grew accustomed to the physical rhythm required to cross massive maps, modern gaming standards have largely evolved toward more ergonomic and seamless movement mappings.

Although specific details regarding the exact new control layout remain to be seen, the confirmation that the traditional face-button sprinting requirement is gone suggests a major quality-of-life update for players navigating the next-generation open world of GTA 6. 

## Editor's Take

Dropping a 25-year-old control convention is a bold yet necessary step for Rockstar. Modern gaming demands fluid and comfortable inputs, and leaving behind the repetitive button-mashing for sprinting will undoubtedly make long exploration sessions much more enjoyable for all players.
